title: What the familiar brought
steps: You have a handful of pieces of black thread in your hand. Above, a bolt is heard, and steps on the back stair.
Rinlo comes out of the arch at the end of the corridor, very pale.
Flying terrifies me. Before every lesson I spend days without sleeping.
That voice found me. I think it felt my fear.
It has been talking to me all year, from the castle's walls, whenever I am alone in a room.
It promised me the flying lessons would stop, it said nobody would get hurt…
…it gave me the threads and taught me to knot them… and then it kept wanting more and more…
…but today I told it I would do nothing more. What it wanted from me could have done you great harm.
Well, that doesn't seem so strange to me, Rinlo… I don't like brooms either.
Rinlo nearly laughs.
The four of you go up to the tower. Orla is alone with the book. You lay the threads on the lectern.
They're threads for tampering with brooms. We have something to tell you…
I must thank you for your honesty.
And for your courage, which is worthy of note in first-year children.
You see, young ones, these threads do far more than tamper with brooms. They are the leavings of a wizard's soul.
A wizard who must have been killed with a black spell. They are evil itself, made a thing by that death.
They cause harm that cannot be told. They draw death and pain. They destroy friendship, and the soul.
"I've had them in a box for months," says {friend}, with hardly any voice.
Loose, they sleep. It is the knot that wakes them.
You did well to untie them, and better to bring them to me.
Orla covers them with a cloth and locks them away.
That knot has not been taught in Arvelia for many years.
You should know that I believe you, and that I trust you.
And to you, Rinlo, I will say: you told it no, you have overcome your fears.
That was the hardest thing, and you have done it.
Treasure the friendships that make you better…
…for only with great friends can any of us reach the place we are called to reach.
There is something you must know, and you more than anyone, {wizard}.

later.13: It takes you a good while to tell the whole story.
